text:
Dov Benyaacov-Kurtzman 
Excuse me, Israeli law does not distinguish family members of Israelis nor family members of non-israelis who live in Israel for touristic entry. According to the law, every non Israeli who wishes to enter Israel for the purpose of a short visit (up to 3 months) could get a tourist visa (other than 4 enemy countries). There isn't such a thing as "regular tourist" or "special tourist". 
There is no clause in PIBA's tourist visa and entry protocol that says family members cannot enter without a prior official invitation/tourist visa application.
What you suggest is to lie to immigration officers. This, in itself, IS actually a stated indication for an entry denial in those protocols.

As a former immigration officer you should know all of that. Although of course, they don't really care about the law there at PIBA.
